title: Etale comparison above a finite flat affine-covered stack
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Deligne--Mumford stacks, representability by algebraic spaces, stacks in groupoids, and 2-fibre products use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]; algebraic spaces use [def-trf-algebraic-space]. A finite flat affine cover of a stack $\mathcal A$ means an affine scheme $U$ and a representable surjective morphism $U\to\mathcal A$ which is finite, flat and locally of finite presentation, tested after scheme base change using [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. A morphism $q:\mathcal A\to M$ to an algebraic space over $S$ is uniform categorical when, for every flat map $M_1\to M$ of algebraic spaces over $S$ and every algebraic space $Z/S$, composition with $q_1:\mathcal A\times_M M_1\to M_1$ is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_S(M_1,Z)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_S(\mathcal A\times_M M_1,Z)$; flatness is tested on scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism]. A morphism of stacks is separated when its relative diagonal is proper, with properness tested on scheme charts using [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let $\mathcal A/S$ and $\mathcal B/S$ be Deligne--Mumford stacks, let $\mathcal A$ admit a finite flat affine cover, and let $q:\mathcal A\to M$ be a uniform categorical morphism with $M$ an affine scheme. Suppose $h:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ is representable, separated and etale, and for every scheme $T/S$ and $b\in\mathcal B(T)$ the map $\operatorname{Aut}_T(b)\to\operatorname{Aut}_T(hb)$ of sheaves is an isomorphism. There are a scheme $N/S$, a separated etale morphism $N\to M$, and an $S$-map $q_B:\mathcal B\to N$ such that the square with rows $h:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ and $N\to M$ and columns $q_B,q$ is 2-cartesian. Etale means [def-weil-etale-morphism] on scheme charts.

source.place: Tag 0DUS, lemma-etale-separated-over-well-nigh-affine, with Tag 0DUR, lemma-moduli-space-finite-affine. Any uniform categorical q with affine target is uniquely isomorphic to the canonical invariant quotient, so the statement is independent of its chosen presentation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-flat-affine-stack-invariant-quotient] to the given affine cover $U\to\mathcal A$. It gives the canonical invariant-spectrum quotient $q_0:\mathcal A\to M_0$. The categorical properties of $q$ and $q_0$ give maps $a:M\to M_0$, $b:M_0\to M$ with $aq=q_0$, $bq_0=q$. Uniqueness gives $ba=1_M$ and $ab=1_{M_0}$. Replace $M_0$ by $M$ using this unique isomorphism. In particular $q$ is a universal homeomorphism, and hence every open substack of $\mathcal A$ is the inverse image of a unique open subscheme of $M$: use the inclusion-preserving open-substack correspondence and the homeomorphism on points. The same assertions apply to each finite-flat affine-covered open stack used below.

Put $V=\mathcal B\times_{\mathcal A}U$. Representability of $h$ makes $V$ an algebraic space, etale over $U$ by chartwise base change. For every scheme test of its relative diagonal, the resulting map is a test of the proper diagonal of $h$, and is universally closed. This remains true after every base change; etale charts detect closed subsets in the point topology of [lem-sfb-space-separated-diagonal-closed]. That criterion gives a closed diagonal, so [lem-a1-separated-etale-space-scheme] makes $V$ a scheme separated etale over $U$. By [lem-a1-etale-space-locally-quasi-finite] it is locally quasi-finite. Thus [lem-sfb-separated-lqf-affine-finite-set] puts every finite subset of $V$ in an affine open. The pulled-back cover $V\to\mathcal B$ is surjective finite flat lfp by its scheme tests. Its kernel pair $R_V$ is a scheme (test this finite cover on $V$); the projections are finite flat lfp, hence finite locally free by [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. By [lem-sfb-fppf-groupoid-stack-presentations](2), $[V/R_V]\simeq\mathcal B$. Each orbit is finite, being the image of a finite source fibre. Apply [lem-sfb-locally-free-groupoid-invariant-affine] to obtain a small cover $V=\bigcup V_i$ by invariant affine opens. By [lem-sfb-finite-flat-groupoid-quotient-open-geometry], applied through the displayed equivalence (so the quotient is Deligne--Mumford), these descend to an open cover $\mathcal B_i$; each $V_i\to\mathcal B_i$ is finite flat lfp surjective, its relation is finite locally free, and $\mathcal B_i\simeq[V_i/R_i]$.

Write $R=U\times_{\mathcal A}U$ and $R_i=V_i\times_{\mathcal B_i}V_i$. The presentation equivalences from step 2 and [lem-sfb-fppf-groupoid-stack-presentations](2), together with the invariant-quotient node, make these affine groupoids with finite locally free source and target. The maps $V_i\to U$ and $R_i\to R$ form a groupoid morphism. Both its source and target squares are cartesian, as can be checked on objects of the 2-fibre products: an object of $V$ is $(b,u,\alpha:hb\simeq pu)$. Given this object and an arrow $r:pu\simeq pu_1$ of $R$, its lifted target is $(b,u_1,r\alpha)$, with identity on $b$. Any other lift is uniquely isomorphic to this one in the fibre product, since an arrow $b\simeq b_1$ with prescribed image under $h$ is unique by representability (faithfulness). This constructs an inverse to the source comparison; interchange endpoints for the target comparison. Restriction to $V_i$ works because its invariance means every such target stays in $V_i$. The stabilizer square is cartesian directly from the assumed automorphism-sheaf isomorphism. Apply [lem-sfb-affine-groupoid-etale-invariant-comparison]: the invariant spectra $N_i\to M$ are etale and $V_i=U\times_MN_i$. It follows also that $R_i=R\times_MN_i$, compatibly with all operations, by the source square. By [lem-sfb-quotient-stack-invariant-base-change] and the presentation equivalences, $\mathcal B_i\simeq\mathcal A\times_MN_i$. Their maps $q_i:\mathcal B_i\to N_i$ are uniform categorical universal homeomorphisms by the invariant-quotient node.

source.place: Tag 0DUQ, presentation and Groupoids 0DT9 argument; corrected relation base change.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal B_{ij}=\mathcal B_i\cap\mathcal B_j$. Since $q_i$ is a universal homeomorphism, its point image is an open $W_{ij}\subseteq N_i$ and $q_i^{-1}W_{ij}=\mathcal B_{ij}$ by the open-substack correspondence. Restriction of uniform categorical $q_i$ to $W_{ij}$ is categorical: this is its flat base change by the open immersion. Similarly obtain $W_{ji}\subseteq N_j$. Their universal properties give unique mutually inverse $\phi_{ij}:W_{ij}\to W_{ji}$ commuting with the maps from $\mathcal B_{ij}$. On triple overlaps the domain is precisely the open corresponding to $\mathcal B_i\cap\mathcal B_j\cap\mathcal B_k$. Both $\phi_{jk}\phi_{ij}$ and $\phi_{ik}$ have the same composite from this stack, so categorical uniqueness gives equality. Likewise $\phi_{ii}=1$ and $\phi_{ji}=\phi_{ij}^{-1}$. These are exactly the open-domain and cocycle conditions of [lem-weil-pbc-glue-schemes]. Glue the $N_i$ to a scheme $N$. The maps $N_i\to M$ agree on overlaps by the same uniqueness, and hence glue to $u:N\to M$.

source.place: Tag 0DUS, overlap and cocycle paragraphs, with the omitted cocycle computation written out.

proof.text: The maps $\mathcal B_i\to N_i\to N$ agree on overlaps by construction of $\phi_{ij}$. For a scheme $T\to\mathcal B$, they give agreeing scheme morphisms on the open covering $T\times_{\mathcal B}\mathcal B_i$; the scheme sheaf axiom glues them to $T\to N$, naturally in $T$. This defines $q_B$. Moreover $q_B^{-1}(N_i)=\mathcal B_i$: on every $\mathcal B_j$, the preimage of $N_i\cap N_j=W_{ji}$ is exactly $\mathcal B_{ji}$. The resulting comparison $\mathcal B\to\mathcal A\times_MN$ restricts over $N_i$ to the equivalence constructed in step 3. Equivalences of stacks are checked on an open cover (full faithfulness is the sheaf condition for isomorphisms; local essential surjectivity glues objects by stack descent), so the comparison is an equivalence. Finally $u$ is etale since its restrictions to the open cover $N_i$ are etale.

source.place: Tag 0DUS, gluing the morphism and checking the cartesian property on the open covering.

proof.text: It remains to prove separatedness. The scheme map $p:V\to N$ restricts over $N_i$ to $V_i\to N_i$. Each is surjective: $V_i\to\mathcal B_i$ and $q_i$ are surjective. It is integral by [lem-a1-affine-groupoid-integral-invariants], and therefore universally closed by [pqf-lem-integral-univclosed]. Surjectivity and universal closedness hold globally for $p$: after any base change, the images of closed sets are closed on the open covering pulled back from the $N_i$, and their union is the global image. The map $V\to M$ is separated: $V\to U$ is separated and $U\to M$ is separated because $U$ is affine, so apply composition of separated morphisms. Now [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-universally-closed-separated] applied to $V\to N\to M$ makes $u$ separated. The square, all structural maps and the gluing are over $S$, as required.
